Somewhat ironically, however. Senate Democrats in November 2013, 
used a procedural maneuver to end the 60-vote requirement to bring 
executive branch and lower court judicial nominations to a vote. Had they 
done so earlier, of course, no recess appointments to the NLRB would have 
been needed in order for President Obama to create a Democratic majority. 
After the Court rendered its decision in Noel Canning, the still Democratic- 
controlled Senate promptly confirmed a slate of Obama nominees to bring 
the NLRB back to full strength.
Tke decision in Noel Conning to treat pro forma sessions as effectively 
delimiting the Senate’s periods of adjournment effectively empowered the 
Senate, either on its own initiative or because triggered by the House, to 
effectively block aU recess appointments. (Technically, Noel Canning did 
not determine whether the ten-day rule apphed also to intersession 
recesses, but Congress can, if it so desires, again limit an intersession 
recess” to the gap between two raps of the gavel.) The Senate’s jealousy of 
its role in appointments may not depend on party control. Although 
Republicans controlled both Houses of Congress during the first half of the 
Donald Trump Administration, the Senate continued to schedule pro forma 
sessions during periods of intrasession recess in order to prevent the 
Republican President from making recess appointments.
Acting Administrators, Presidents, however, may not need recess 
appointments in order to insure their continued pohtical influence over an 
agency even after a key position becomes vacant. Many agency statutes 
contain provisions that indicate who automatically fills specific positions 
that become vacant, sometimes also authorizing the President to designate 
another choice. In addition. Congress, through the so-called Federal 
Vacancies Reform Act (FVRA), 5 U.S.C. §§ 3345-3349d, authorizes the 
president in most cases to fiR vacancies in advice-and-consent positions 
with temporary “acting” administrators. The FVRA did not help President 
Obama with the NLRB because it does not apply to the position of ^^any 
member who is appointed by the president, by and with the advice and 
consent of the Senate to any board, commission, or similar entity that
(A) 
is cornposed of multiple members; and (B) governs an independent 
establishment or Government corporation.” 5 U.S.C. § 3349c. With regard 
to some multimember agencies. Congress has dealt with the potential 
vacancy problem caused by appointment delays by allowing officers to 
serve beyond their terms until the confirmation of their successors, e.g., 2 
U.S.C. § 437c (Federal Election Commission); 19 U.S.C. § 13300)) 
(International Trade Commission). NLRB members, however, do not enjoy 
this privilege. 29 U.S.C. § 153.
